A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Curse of Depth and LayerNorm Scaling research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLaMA pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, layer-pruning experiments, and activation-variance analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds larger-model training, representation analyses, vision experiments, multimodal pruning, and ablations.

M1.justification: The language-model method retains the same inverse-square-root layer-index scaling after normalization in Equation 12. V2 adds a vision-specific adaptation that places scaling after attention/MLP blocks instead of after LayerNorm (Section 5.6).

E1.justification: V2 extends the retained language-task coverage to ImageNet-1K image classification with ViT-S and MMMU multimodal evaluation with Qwen2.5-VL-7B (Section 5.6 and Appendix C). These introduce image and multimodal task requirements absent from v1.

E2.justification: The scaling comparison expands from LayerScale and Scaled Initialization in v1 Table 4 to include SkipInit and Depth-Scaled Initialization in v2 Table 6. V2 also evaluates OLMo's initialization against LNS in Table 3, substantially expanding comparisons with alternative scaling procedures. Existing normalization comparators remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include OLMo models from 60M to 7B trained on a fixed 20B-token budget, Qwen2.5-0.5B trained for 6B tokens, angular-distance measurements averaged over 256K C4 tokens, and a matched LLaMA-130M Pre-LN/Post-LN control. Vision evaluation adds top-1 accuracy with LayerScale removed. The retained LLaMA pre-training budgets and learning rates are unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds representation-similarity analyses, controlled normalization comparisons, scaling-placement ablations, an LNS-plus-initialization compatibility test, and modality-specific pruning analyses. These investigate layer redundancy, component placement, and applicability beyond the pruning and variance analyses already present in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's averaging over 256K tokens specifies metric sampling, rather than introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the fine-tuning table retain their scores. Newly reported results include OLMo-1B loss of 2.96 versus 2.85 for OLMo initialization versus LNS, and Qwen2.5 perplexity of 20.62 versus 19.57 for Pre-LN versus LNS. V2 also adds vision, angular-distance, and multimodal findings. Qwen3 pruning is added, while Mistral-7B, Qwen-7B, LLaMA2-7B pruning plots and the old LLaMA-1B loss curve are omitted.

T1.justification: V2 adds Theorem 4.3 on parameter-gradient bounds with Appendix A.5, and a formal softmax-concentration lemma in Appendix A.1. It revises dimensional factors in the attention-variance derivation and changes the scaling-bound epsilon range from (0, 1/4] to [1/2, 1). V1's brief Post-LN variance analysis is removed.

C1.justification: The central Pre-LN explanation and LNS remedy remain. V2 extends the abstract's advertised pre-training range from 130M–1B to 130M–7B, drops the introduction's half-training-tokens claim, and adds a 66%-fewer-parameters claim in Figure 1. These refine the performance and efficiency claims without replacing the main contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations involving representation diversity, parameter-gradient stability, and interference from scaled initialization. It qualifies transfer to vision through placement-dependent benefits and distinguishes vision from language branches in multimodal models. Appendix D adds substantive architectural, task-coverage, and representation-quality limitations absent from v1.

D1.justification: V2 supplies OLMo initialization formulas, recommends removing scaled initialization when adopting LNS, and specifies removing LayerScale in the vision experiments. These add practical implementation information without establishing changes to the retained LLaMA runs. The code repository link is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of DyT, HybridNorm, SkipInit, and additional initialization and gradient-spike literature while retaining the central research positioning. DyT and HybridNorm are discussed rather than evaluated. Much of the apparent expansion of related work comes from relocating the existing deep-layer-redundancy discussion from the introduction.

P1.justification: The introduction and empirical-evidence section are substantially rewritten and reorganized. Existing normalization and scaling comparisons move into a dedicated ablation section, the introductory literature discussion moves to related work, and the Impact Statement disappears. These narrative changes accompany new scaling, vision, and limitations sections.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text from two columns to one, adds a separate title page and contents page, and combines the existing method schematic with a new scaling plot. Pruning figures gain heatmaps, and new experimental tables and vision/multimodal plots appear. Existing variance plots and several tables are relocated or expanded rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: V2's matched Pre-LN/Post-LN pruning comparison addresses architectural confounding in v1's BERT-versus-LLM evidence. Representation diagnostics, larger-model experiments, and placement/initialization ablations substantially strengthen the empirical case, while modality-specific findings and explicit limitations clarify applicability. These gains outweigh the reporting weaknesses, although the mismatch between Theorem 4.3 and Appendix A.5's final expression limits the added theoretical support, and Table 4's caption describes LLaMA runs absent from its rows.
